verdict.rationale: Kong AI Gateway's AI Auth Strategy entity declares an inbound authentication mechanism and attaches it to specific AI Models, AI Agents, or AI MCP Servers, which gives a form of per-resource scoping for agent access. OIDC-based IdP authentication is also documented. However, the evidence never shows the gateway issuing a distinct credential for an agent or defining fine-grained scopes or permissions on that credential. Missing for 10: documented issuance of per-agent API keys or tokens, explicit scope/permission definitions on credentials, least-privilege examples, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: An AI Auth Strategy lets you declare an inbound authentication mechanism at the gateway level and attach it to specific AI Models, AI Agents, or AI MCP Servers.
Authenticate enterprise users through an existing identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, Google, or any OIDC-compliant IdP) without managing keys manually
Reference an AI Auth Strategy on your AI Agent entities to authenticate A2A clients
